The 3 macronutrients crude balance are deﬁned as:
Carbohydrate balance ¼ carbohydrate intake  carbohydrate oxidation
LipidðFatÞ balance ¼ lipidðfatÞ intake  lipidðfatÞ oxidation
Protein balance ¼ protein intake  protein oxidation
There is a direct mathematical relationship between total energy balance and total macronutrient balance, since the arithmetic
sum of individual substrates balance (when macronutrients are expressed as energy) is equivalent to the overall energy balance.
Note that the importance of lipid (fat) balance concept merits more details, given in a subsequent paragraph.
318
Energy balance


In a study composed of heterogeneous individuals (both lean and obese ones pooled), energy balance calculated over a period
of weeks, was well correlated to total fat balance. This indicates that when there is an increase in body energy stores due to positive
energy balance, this was mostly explained by body fat accumulation in adipose tissue rather than increase in muscles.
Total body energy stores (constituted mainly of fat stores in adipose tissue) represent a large proportion of the total daily energy
ingested. For example, let’s take a 60 kg non-obese woman (with 25% body fat), who is eating 2000 kcal/day), this would represent
a total adipose tissue storage (at 8000 kcal/kg for fat) of 120,000 kcal. Hence, this represents theoretically 60 days of fat available
stored, whereas carbohydrate storage (as glycogen) constitutes only 3–4 days of reserve.
